And putting all his money in the bank. <break time="0.8s" /> He studied the newspaper advertisements for country estates. <break time="0.8s" /> Every day and in every farm he imagined. <break longer young. <break time="0.8s" /> Nikolai married an elderly, unattractive widow. <break time="0.8s" /> Not out of love. <break time="0.8s" /> But because she had saved a fair amount of money. <break time="0.8s" /> He kept her half starved. <break time="0.8s" /> Putting her money in the bank. <break time="0.8s" /> Under his own name. <break time="0.8s" /> And she. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had once lived comfortably. <break time="0.8s" /> Slowly grew pale and thin. <break time="0.8s" /> Within three years she died. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet Nikolai never for a moment believed. <break time="0.8s" /> He was to blame. <break time="0.8s" /> For, as Ivan Ivanych said. <break time="0.8s" /> Money, like vodka. <break time="0.8s" /> Can make a man strange. <break time="0.8s" /> At last Nikolai bought an estate. <break time="0.8s" /> Of about three hundred acres. <break time="0.8s" /> A mortgaged property. <break time="0.8s" /> That had no orchard, no duck pond. <break time="0.8s" /> And not a single gooseberry bush. <break time="0.8s" /> Through it flowed a river. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose water was the color of coffee. <break time="0.8s" /> Because a brickworks. <break ordered twenty gooseberry bushes. <break time="0.8s" /> Planted them. <break time="0.8s" /> And settled down to live as a landowner.
